gain.label: Gain versus loss framing: Gain frame
gain.reported_description: Programs described by lives saved (Program A / Program B)
gain.participant_text:
Imagine that the United States is preparing for the outbreak of an unusual disease, which is expected to kill 600 people. Two alternative programs to fight the disease have been proposed. Assume that the exact scientific estimate of the consequences of the program are as follows:
If Program A is adopted, 200 people will be saved 
If Program B is adopted, there is 1/3 probability that 600 people will be saved and 2/3 probability that no people will be saved.
Which program would you choose?
Choose program:
Program A
Program B

loss.label: Gain versus loss framing: Loss frame
loss.reported_description: Programs described by lives lost (Program C / Program D)
loss.participant_text:
Imagine that the United States is preparing for the outbreak of an unusual disease, which is expected to kill 600 people. Two alternative programs to fight the disease have been proposed. Assume that the exact scientific estimate of the consequences of the program are as follows:  If Program C is adopted, 400 people will die.   If Program D is adopted, there is 1/3 probability that no people will die and 2/3 probability that 600 people will die.  Which program would you choose?
Choose program:
Program C
Program D

s03.name: Study 3: Anchoring

response_format.instruction: (Implementation instruction, not printed material) Put your four estimates after ANSWER:, as plain numbers separated by semicolons, in the order the questions appear.

low.label: Anchoring: Low anchor
low.reported_description: Receives a low anchor value before estimating
low.participant_text:
We are interested in people's beliefs about the world around them. For each of the following 4 questions we would like you to give your best estimate. If you do not know the correct answer, just give your best guess.

The distance from San Francisco to New York City is longer than 1,500 miles. How far do you think it is?
(miles)

The population of Chicago is more than 200,000. What do you think the population of Chicago is?
(people)

Mount Everest is taller than 2,000 feet. How tall do you think Mount Everest is?
(feet)

More than 100 babies are born per day in the United States. How many babies do you think are born in the U.S. each day?
(babies)

high.label: Anchoring: High anchor
high.reported_description: Receives a high anchor value before estimating
high.participant_text:
We are interested in people's beliefs about the world around them. For each of the following 4 questions we would like you to give your best estimate. If you do not know the correct answer, just give your best guess.

The distance from San Francisco to New York City is shorter than 6,000 miles. How far do you think it is?
(miles)

The population of Chicago is less than 5,000,000. What do you think the population of Chicago is?
(people)

Mount Everest is shorter than 45,500 feet. How tall do you think Mount Everest is?
(feet)

Less than 50,000 babies are born per day in the United States. How many babies do you think are born in the U.S. each day?
(babies)

s03.notes: The document lists the eight items in random order, one per page; the replay shows each participant the four topics in a fixed order so replies can be parsed. Answer-box units are from the study pages (the document labels the high SF–NY box '(babies)'; see issue i_s03_unit_label).
